children: New Delhi, Oct. 25 -- Are you aiming to build a meaningful corpus for your future? Do you have a proper financial plan to accomplish the same objective? Are you aware of the silent power of compounding?

Having a clear understanding of these basic concepts is indispensable for ensuring meaningful wealth creation in the long run. Now, building a corpus of Rs.1 crore through mutual fund investments may seem a challenging and daunting task; still, a disciplined approach, clarity of objectives and a long-term investment horizon can help investors work towards this goal.

The 15-15-15 rule of investing is a popular investment thumb rule that clearly explains how patience, consistency in investing, time, and compounding can work together to build wealth in the long run. This write-up is dedicated to discussing this rule in detail and how it can help create meaningful wealth if followed diligently.

This is an investment rule that suggests investing Rs.15,000 every month through SIPs, i.e., a Systematic Investment Plan, targeting an assumed annual return of 15% over an extended period of 15 years. Furthermore, the returns under this rule are reinvested, allowing the investment corpus to benefit from compounding.

Still, it is vital to note that the 15-15-15 rule does not guarantee a Rs.1 crore corpus in 15 years. This is because market returns are subject to risks and depend on a host of other factors. Secondly, at a 15% annualised return, which is a presumed return, the estimated corpus would be approximately Rs.1 crore, depending on the calculation method, timing of investments and eventual compounding value.

These figures assume monthly investments and an annualised return of 15%. The returns under this investment are compounded monthly. The presumed returns here are instructive in nature. Further, the actual returns will vary with market performance and the timing of investments.

For investors, it is very important to acknowledge and understand that a 15% return is only an assumption. It is not an assured return. Equity markets, stocks or mutual funds are market-linked investment products, and their value can fluctuate immensely depending on aspects such as geopolitical conditions, oil and commodity prices, etc.
